clue.text: The parties are on live, moreover

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
the parties to a dispute or contest are its sides

explanation.surface: Someone notes the party is still going, and adds a remark besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are on' simply links the two pieces; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are sentence adverbs adding a further point, as in 'and also'.

clue.text: Bloke with family of 27, possibly?

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person, a bloke
kin are one's relatives, family

explanation.surface: A man with a big family of twenty-seven children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the wordplay to the definition, which points to 27 across, NEEDLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunt, large-eyed implement for threading tape through fabric is a type of sewing needle.

clue.text: Ray is armed to the teeth

definitions.text: Ray is armed to the teeth

parts.words: Ray is armed to the teeth
parts.note: not a man called Ray carrying weapons but a ray fish whose long snout is edged with teeth like a cutting blade

explanation.surface: A man called Ray carries enough weapons for a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'armed to the teeth' is the idiom for heavily armed; literally the fish's weapon is lined with teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: This elongated ray has a flat snout fringed with teeth like a carpenter's toothed blade.

clue.text: Bay, for example, that may appear from nowhere

definitions.text: Bay, for example, that may appear from nowhere

parts.words: Bay, for example, that may appear from nowhere
parts.note: a bay is a brown horse, and an unfancied runner may come from nowhere to win

explanation.surface: A coastal inlet seems to materialise out of thin air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' suggests a stretch of coast; it is a reddish-brown horse, and the phrase is for an unexpected winner or candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A little-known contender who unexpectedly succeeds is named after an unknown racehorse.

clue.text: .One helps a striker to spot deliveries

definitions.text: One helps a striker to spot deliveries

parts.words: One helps a striker to spot deliveries
parts.note: in cricket a large white board behind the bowler helps the batsman see the ball coming

explanation.surface: Someone assists a worker on strike in noticing parcels arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman (striker) faces deliveries from the bowler; a large white board behind the bowler lets the ball be seen. The leading dot in the held clue is a stray mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A movable white screen at a cricket ground gives the batter a clear background against which to see the ball.

clue.text: One of twin arches raised by the superior

definitions.text: One of twin arches raised by the superior

parts.words: One of twin arches raised by the superior
parts.note: a haughty, supercilious person lifts one of the paired arcs of hair above the eyes in disdain

explanation.surface: A grand double archway is erected on the orders of a monastic superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arches' suggests architecture and 'superior' a religious head; really a superior person raises one in scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched line of hair above each eye comes in a pair, and a raised one signals condescension.

clue.text: Swallow nestling in the attic

indicators.note: nestling in says the letters sit snugly within the words the attic

explanation.surface: A swallow has made its nest up in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird, helped by 'nestling'; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow food is to consume or ingest it.

clue.text: Poet needs energy to work standing up

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word for work is read from bottom to top

parts.note: toil means hard work

explanation.surface: A poet must find the energy to write at a standing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns TOIL into LIOT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot, author of The Waste Land, is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Sales slip, we hear, with eccentric Peter in charge

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: A customer hears about a sale's paperwork with odd Peter running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges PETER together with IC; 'we hear' only links, perhaps noting the silent P.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip given at a sale is a written acknowledgment that payment has been made.

clue.text: Air-hose for runway use?

parts.note: not a tube for compressed air but a hosiery item for the air, a cloth cone filled by the breeze at an airfield

explanation.surface: An airport needs a compressed-air pipe on the tarmac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' also means stockings, so an 'air-hose' is a fabric tube the breeze fills to show its direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric cone on a pole at an airfield shows pilots the direction and strength of the breeze.

clue.text: Plain area of rolling land, ideal

parts.note: a down is an area of open rolling chalk hill country, as in the South Downs of England
the ideal choice is the right one

explanation.surface: A description of perfect flat countryside with gently rolling hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a noun for flat land beside 'rolling land', but it is the adjective meaning utter or frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain in the sense of sheer or unmistakable, as in 'plain rudeness', is a synonym.

clue.text: Quechuan, perhaps, recorded?

definitions.meaning: Quechua was the language of the Andean empire ruled from Cuzco, so a Quechua speaker might belong to that people
a finished film or recording is said to be 'in the can'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a South American language has been recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Quechua speakers include the descendants of the Andean empire's people; a completed take is 'in the can', i.e. recorded.

clue.text: Flag his first in race

parts.note: a flag is a yellow iris, the waterside plant

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word his

explanation.surface: A man's flag flies first in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is not a banner but the plant also called the yellow iris. 'in' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Ireland can be called a race or nation, as in 'the Irish'.

clue.text: Stagy effects of their acts in variety

indicators.note: in variety says the letters of their acts appear in a varied, rearranged form

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: Performers' showy routines in a variety show are over-the-top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' looks like the music-hall setting of the acts, but here it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, exaggerated behaviour or theatrical effects are described with this plural noun.

clue.text: Sparks nice article off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: A pleasant newspaper piece is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparks' is British slang for the tradesman who wires houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is a nickname for a tradesman who installs wiring, from the flashes of current.

clue.text: Typical of part of a logarithm

definitions.meaning: typical of something means distinctive of it
in mathematics the integer part of a common logarithm has this name, the decimal part being the mantissa

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that something is typical of a logarithm.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinctive or typical is the adjective sense; the whole-number portion of a logarithm is the technical noun sense.

clue.text: Take a hand to bury, even when broken up

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body

indicators.note: broken up means the letters of the word even are split apart and reassembled

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone helps to bury something, even though it has been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' links the two pieces; 'broken up' turns EVEN into VENE.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a hand in a matter is to involve oneself and step in.

clue.text: Pavilion here for brilliant cricket side

parts.note: bright means brilliant, shining
the on side, or leg side, is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket pavilion hosts a brilliant team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pavilion' suggests a cricket clubhouse; it is the Royal Pavilion, an English seaside town's oriental-style palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Pavilion, George IV's exotic palace, stands in this south-coast English resort.

clue.text: Agent of 14?

definitions.meaning: an agent acts on someone's behalf, as a delegate
the answer to 14 across means typical, so 'typical of' is reworded

explanation.surface: A spy is asked to identify himself by number.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition substitutes 14 across, CHARACTERISTIC, as an adjective: 'characteristic of' means typical of.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate acting for others is one sense; being typical or illustrative of a class is the other.

clue.text: Dog-star

definitions.meaning: a gundog breed that stands rigid indicating game
either of the two stars in the Plough that line up with the Pole Star

explanation.surface: The Dog Star, Sirius, is named.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes 'Dog-star' look like Sirius; it is two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting dog that indicates game is one sense; one of two stars in the Plough lining up with Polaris is the other.

clue.text: How like plants, to catch in calf's flesh

indicators.note: in places the word for catch inside the word for calf meat

parts.note: veal is the meat of a calf
to get a ball or an illness is to catch it

explanation.surface: Someone asks how plants manage to snare something inside a calf's meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the definition to the wordplay; 'calf's flesh' suggests the leg, but it is VEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to or resembling vegetation is the adjective's meaning, so 'how like plants' asks for it.

clue.text: Vessel taking in Barcelona, say, for the games?

indicators.note: taking in places the harbour word inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel
Barcelona is an example of a seaport

explanation.surface: A cruise ship calls at Barcelona so passengers can see the Olympic games.
explanation.walkthrough: Barcelona hosted the 1992 Olympics, so it suggests the games; here it is just a seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic events and contests collectively are called sports or games.

clue.text: Sliding scales for musicians

parts.note: not pay rates that vary but rapid runs of notes slid through on an instrument, the Italian plural of a musical term

explanation.surface: Variable pay rates are being arranged for orchestra players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sliding scales' suggests flexible charges or wages; read literally, it is notes glided through in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: These are rapid slides up or down a run of notes, the Italian-styled plural of the musical term.

clue.text: Soil's disturbed to make storage-pits

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: Dug-up earth is used to create pits for storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pits or towers for storing grain or fodder are known by this name.

clue.text: Hurriedly improvise riding gear first

indicators.note: first says the gear piece is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: rig is equipment or gear, as in a drilling rig or a sailor's rigging
a jockey who is riding is said to be 'up'

explanation.surface: Someone must quickly cobble together riding kit before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riding gear' reads as one phrase for saddlery, but it splits: a jockey who is riding is said to be 'up', and 'first' puts the gear in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up something makeshift in a hurry is a phrasal verb for jury-building or knocking together.

clue.text: What is the final score, all out?

definitions.meaning: the sum reached when every figure is added together
complete or unrestricted, as in all-out war

explanation.surface: A cricket fan asks what the final score was once the side was dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a side is 'all out' when ten batsmen are dismissed, so the surface reads as one question about a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum at the end is one sense; complete and thoroughgoing, as in an all-out effort, is the other.

clue.text: Spruce trees replanted for the academic term

parts.note: spruce as an adjective or verb means neat, tidy: trim

indicators.note: replanted says the letters of trees are set down again in a new order

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: Conifers are moved to new beds during the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like the tree beside 'trees', but it means neat; 'replanted' turns TREES into ESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A term at some schools and colleges lasting about three months, one third of the year, especially in the US.

clue.text: Marijuana that comes from pot?

definitions.meaning: an old slang term for cannabis
a drink poured from a teapot

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether cannabis is really derived from pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' looks like more cannabis slang; it is the teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: Old drug slang called cannabis by this name; the hot drink is poured from a pot.

clue.text: Italian barmaid's assistant, retired as temptress

indicators.note: retired means drew back, so the combined word pair is read backwards

parts.note: a siren is a seductive woman, from the singers of Greek myth

explanation.surface: An assistant to an Italian bar worker has quit, branded a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Italian barmaid' is Portia of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, who pleads at the bar as a lawyer; 'retired' turns AS SIREN back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play the Belmont heiress who poses as a lawyer has a waiting-woman by this name.

clue.text: Near-redundant sewers

indicators.note: near means almost, so the word for redundant falls just short of complete, missing its final letter

parts.note: redundant means unnecessary, superfluous

explanation.surface: Drains that are almost no longer needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' looks like drains; it means things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp implements used for stitching are literally things that sew.
